newsitem.title: CHINA: China to finish Pakistan nuclear plant in 97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: China to finish Pakistan nuclear plant in 97 - paper.

text.p: China is expected to complete installation of a 300-megawatt nuclear power station in Pakistan before the end of this year, the China Daily said on Monday.
Officials have said work on the Chashma plant in Pakistan's central province of Punjab was due to be completed in 1998, with the power station to be handed over to Pakistan authorities in March 1999.
"Installation...is expected to be completed during (this) year," China Daily quoted China National Nuclear Corp spokesman You Deliang as saying.

The official newspaper did not say if the handover of the plant, being built near the Jhelum river, 280 km (170 miles) south of Islamabad, was likely to be brought forward if construction was completed ahead of schedule.
Work on the plant, which is being built under International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards, began in 1993.
Pakistan said last month that China was willing in principle to provide Islamabad with a second Chashma nuclear plant, but that the financing had not yet been arranged.
The United States has urged China to stop all nuclear cooperation with Pakistan, which Washington suspects is trying to develop a nuclear weapons capability to match that of its neighbour, India.
Beijing has repeatedly said it provides nuclear technology to Pakistan for peaceful uses.
